title: A Quantum Approach to Vagueness and to the Semantics of Music
abstract: Quantum computational logics represent a suitable abstract environment for modelling semantic situations where vagueness and ambiguity play a relevant role. In this framework vague possible worlds can be described as a kind of abstract scenes, where individual concepts, relational concepts and events behave as quantum-like superpositions that ambiguously allude to a number of possibly antagonistic alternatives. The quantum semantics can be naturally applied to a formal analysis of musical compositions, where both musical ideas and extra-musical meanings are characterized by some essentially vague and ambiguous features. We investigate some examples.
text: <title>A Quantum Approach to Vagueness and to the Semantics of Music<abstract>Quantum computational logics represent a suitable abstract environment for modelling semantic situations where vagueness and ambiguity play a relevant role. In this framework vague possible worlds can be described as a kind of abstract scenes, where individual concepts, relational concepts and events behave as quantum-like superpositions that ambiguously allude to a number of possibly antagonistic alternatives. The quantum semantics can be naturally applied to a formal analysis of musical compositions, where both musical ideas and extra-musical meanings are characterized by some essentially vague and ambiguous features. We investigate some examples.<Introduction>It has been often recognized that semantical theories based on classical logic represent an unsatisfactory tool for an adequate analysis of natural and of artistic languages. The main reason depends on two strong principles that underlie classical semantics: -the compositionality-principle, according to which the meaning of any well-formed expression of a given language is determined by the meanings of its well-formed parts (from the parts to the whole). -Theexcluded-middle principle, according to which any sentence of a language is either true or false in any possible world that represents an admitted interpretation of the language. Both these principles are often violated in the common use of natural and of artistic languages, where meanings generally behave in a holistic and contextual way: the meaning of a global expression determines the contextual meanings of its parts (from the whole to the parts). Furthermore, properties and relations may be vague and ambiguous, giving rise to possible violations both of the excluded-middle and of the non-contradiction principle.<Quantum Computational Logics and Vague Possible Worlds>Quantum computation has suggested a new form of quantum semantics that represents a suitable abstract framework for modelling situations where vagueness, ambiguity, holism and contextuality play an important role. 1 Let us briefly recall the basic features of a quantum computational semantics for a firstorder language L, whose non-logical alphabet contains individual terms (variables and names), predicates and sentential constants. Interpreting the language L means associating to any formula α a meaning, identified with a piece of quantum information that can be stored by a quantum system. Accordingly, any possible meaning of α is represented by a possible (pure or mixed) state of a quantum system: generally, a density operator ρ α that lives in a Hilbert space H α , whose dimension depends on the linguistic complexity of α. The logical operators of L are associated to special examples of Hilbert-space operations that have a characteristic dynamic behavior, representing possible computation-actions. The logical connectives are interpreted as particular (reversible) unitary quantum operations, corresponding to some important quantum-logical gates, like the negation NOT, the Toffoligate T (which allows us to define a reversible conjunction AND), the Hadamard-gate I, which transforms classical pieces of information (bits and registers) into genuine pieces of quantum information (qubits and quregisters). At the same time, the logical quantifiers (∀, ∃) are interpreted as possibly irreversible quantum operations. Since the universe of discourse (which the language refers to) may be indeterminate, the use of quantum quantifiers may give rise to a reversibility-breaking, which is quite similar to what happens in the case of measurement-phenomena. Whenever the universe of discourse is determinate and finite, any use of a universal quantifier can be dealt with by means of a multiple finite application of the reversible conjunction AND. Due to the characteristic features of quantum holism, meanings turn out to behave in a holistic and contextual way: the density operator ρ α (which represents the global meaning of a formula α) determines the contextual meanings of all parts of α. As expected, the contextual meaning of any part of α (whose global meaning is ρ α ) can be obtained by applying the reduced-state function to ρ α . As a consequence, it may happen that the meaning of a formula is an entangled pure state, while the meanings of its parts are proper mixtures. In such cases, the meaning of a global expression turns out to be more precise than the meanings of its parts (against the compositionality-principle). It is also admitted that one and the same formula receives different contextual meanings in different contexts. As an example, consider the atomic sentence "Alice is pretty" (formalized as Pa). In order to store the information expressed by this sentence, we need three quantum objects whose states represent the pieces of information corresponding, respectively, to the predicate P, to the name a and to the truth-degree according to which the individual denoted by the name a satisfies the property denoted by the predicate P. Accordingly, the meaning of the sentence Pa can be identified with a (pure or mixed) state ρ Pa living in the tensorproduct space In order to obtain the contextual meanings of the linguistic parts of Pa it is sufficient to consider the two reduced states red 1 (ρ Pa ) and red 2 (ρ Pa ), which describe (respectively) the states of the first and of the second subsystem of the quantum object that stores the information expressed by the sentence Pa. From a logical point of view, red 1 (ρ Pa ) and red 2 (ρ Pa ) can be regarded as two intensional meanings: a property-concept and an individual concept, respectively; while ρ Pa represents a propositional concept (or event). Notice that, unlike most semantic approaches, we do not assume here any ontological hierarchy between individuals and properties: states of the space C 2 can store either individual names or predicates. For instance, the meaning ρ Pa might correspond to the following factorized pure state: where |0 and |1 (the elements of the canonical orthonormal basis of C 2 ) represent, in this framework, the truth-values Falsity and Truth (or, equivalntly, the two classical bits). Since 1 √ 2 (|0 + |1 ) corresponds to an intermediate truth-degree between the Falsity and the Truth, one obtains that Alice (the individual described by the qubit |ϕ ) satisfies the property described by the qubit |ψ with probability-value 1 2 . In the context | , "prettiness" turns out to be a fully vague property of Alice. Of course, any form of vagueness essentially depends on the choice of the basis of the space C 2 (whose elements represent the Falsity and the Truth). Changing the basis gives rise to a change of truth-perspective, which may transform vague properties into sharp properties (or viceversa). From a physical point of view, different truth-perspectives may correspond to different choices of observables that can be measured. Consider, for instance, the Bell-basis and suppose that 1 ) represent the Falsity and the Truth, respectively. In such a case, Alice turns out to satisfy the prettiness-property with probabilityvalue 0 (in the context | Pa ). So far we have considered the case of an atomic sentence. In a similar way, one can assign meanings to molecular formulas that may contain either logical connectives or quantifiers. To this aim, one shall use the corresponding quantum operations in an appropriate way. Consider, for instance, the following sentence: "Alice is not pretty" (formalized as ¬Pa). As expected, the connective ¬ shall be interpreted as the gate NOT, the unitary operator that is defined as follows on the canonical basis of the space Cfoot_1 : Definition 1 (The Negation-gate) Accordingly, any interpretation that assigns, for instance, to the sentence Pa the meaning will assign to the negated sentence ¬Pa the meaning (where I is the identity operator of the space C 2 ). Since Alice's "prettiness" has been interpreted as a vague property, it is not strange that both the sentence Pa and its negation ¬Pa turn out to have one and the same meaning In fact, the non-contradiction principle is generally violated in quantum computational logics. 2 The logical operators of the quantum computational semantics generally behave in a holistic way. As an example, consider the following conjunctive sentence: "Alice is beautiful and good". For the sake of simplicity, let us formalize this sentence as the conjunction b ∧ g of two sentential constants (b, g). Accordingly, all possible meanings either of b or of g will live in the space C 2 . From an intuitive point of view, the conjunction of the concepts "beauty" and "goodness" may recall the famous expression "καλòς καγ αθ óς " ("beautiful and good") often mentioned by ancient Greek writers and philosophers (from Homer to Aristotle), who also termed "καλoκαγ αθíα" the corresponding abstract virtue. The authors who used such linguistic contractions seemed to stress how the conjunction "beauty and goodness" cannot be reduced to a mere combination of the two separate concepts ("beauty", "goodness"). In the quantum computational semantics the logical conjunction AND is defined in terms of the Toffoli-gate T. Consider the Hilbert space ⊗ 3 C 2 . The gate T is the unitary operator that is defined as follows on the elements |x, y, z of the canonical basis of ⊗ 3 C 2 : Definition 2 (The Toffoli-gate) T|x, y, z := |x, y, x • y + z (where + is the addition modulo 2). On this basis, the holistic conjunction AND can be defined as an abbreviation for a special application of the Toffoli-gate. For any state |ψ of the space (where the bit |0 plays the role of an ancilla). Apparently, AND represents a reversible generalization of the classical conjunction. For, we have: The Toffoli-gate T can be naturally generalized to any space having the following form: Furthermore, both T and the conjunction AND can be canonically extended to density operators (as happens in the case of all unitary operators). On this basis, any conjunctive formula α ∧ β of the language L can be interpreted as a density operator ρ α∧β that lives in a Hilbert space H α∧β determined by the linguistic complexity of the component formulas (α, β). In order to realize how the conjunction AND generally behaves in a holistic way, consider a particular interpretation for the sentence b ∧ g ("Alice is beautiful and good"). Suppose that our interpretation has assigned to the sentence-pair (b, g) the following global meaning: which is an entangled state of the space In such a case, the conjunction b ∧ g will receive the following interpretation: Consequently, "beauty and goodness" ("καλoκαγ αθíα") represents a vague property that is satisfied by Alice with probability-value The global meaning of a conjunction cannot be generally represented as a conjunction of its separate parts! Like formulas, sequences of formulas also can be interpreted according to the quantum computational rules. As expected, a possible meaning of the sequence (α 1 , . . . , α n ) will be a density operator ρ (α 1 ,...,α n ) living in a Hilbert space H (α 1 ,...,α n ) , whose dimension depends on the linguistic complexity of the formulas α 1 , . . . , α n . In this framework one can develop an abstract theory of vague possible worlds. Consider a pair consisting of a sequence of formulas and of a density operator that represents a possible meaning for our sequence. It seems reasonable to assume that W describes a vague possible world, a kind of abstract scene where most events are characterized by a "cloud of ambiguities", due to quantum uncertainties. In some cases W might be exemplified as a "real" scene of a theatrical play or as a vague situation that is described either in a novel or in a poem. And it is needless to recall how ambiguities play an essential role in literary works. As an example, consider the following vague possible world: where Pab is supposed to formalize the sentence "Alice is kissing Bob", while ρ Pab corresponds to the pure state where |ϕ lives in the space C 2 , while | Pab lives in the space ⊗ 4 C 2 . Here the reduced state of | Pab that describes the pair (Alice, Bob) is an entangled Bell-state; consequently, the states describing the two individuals Alice and Bob are two identical mixed states. In the context | Pab Alice and Bob turn out to be indistinguishable: it is not determined "who is who" and "who is kissing whom". It is not difficult to imagine some "real" theatrical scenes representing ambiguous situations of this kind.<A Quantum-Like Semantics for Music>An abstract version of the quantum computational semantics can be applied to a formal analysis of musical compositions, where both musical ideas and extra-musical meanings are generally characterized by some essentially vague and ambiguous features. 3 Any musical composition (say, a sonata, a symphony, a lyric opera,...) is, generally, determined by three elements: -a score; -a set of performances; -a set of musical thoughts (or ideas), which represent possible meanings for the musical phrases written in the score. While scores represent the syntactical component of musical compositions, performances are physical events that occur in space and time. From a logical point of view, we could say that performances are, in a sense, similar to extensional meanings, i.e. well determined systems of objects which the linguistic expressions refer to. Musical thoughts (or ideas) represent, instead, a mysterious element. Is it really sensible to assume the existence of such ideal objects that are, in a sense, similar to the intensional meanings investigated by logic? Is there any danger to adhere, in this way, to a form of Platonism? When discussing semantic questions, one should not be "afraid" of Platonism. In the particular case of music, a composition cannot be simply reduced to a score and to a system of sound-events. Between a score (which is a system of signs) and the sound-events created by a performance there is something intermediate, represented by the musical ideas that underlie the different performances. This is the abstract environment where normally live both composers and conductors, who are accustomed to study scores without any help of a material instrument. Following the rules of the quantum semantics, musical ideas can be naturally represented as superpositions that ambiguously describe a variety of co-existent thoughts. Accordingly, we can write: where: -|μ is an abstract object representing a musical idea that alludes to other ideas |μ i (possible variants of |μ that are, in a sense, all co-existent); -the number c i measures the "weigth" of the component |μ i in the context |μ . As happens in the case of composite quantum systems, musical ideas (which represent possible meanings of musical phrases written in a score) have an essential holistic behaviour: the meaning of a global musical phrase determines the contextual meanings of all its parts (and not the other way around). As an example, we can refer to the notion of musical theme. What exactly are musical themes? Generally a theme appears in a musical composition with different "masks". In some cases it can be easily recognized even in its transformations; sometimes it is disguised and can be hardly discovered. Of course, a theme cannot be identified with a particular (syntactical) phrase written in the score; for, any theme essentially alludes to a (potentially) infinite set of possible variants. One is dealing with a vague musical idea that cannot be either played or written. At the same time, it is interesting to investigate (by scientific methods) the musical parameters that represent a kind of invariant, characteristic of a given theme. In different situations the relevant parameters may concern the melody or the harmony or the rhythm or the timbre. The ambiguous correlations between a theme and its possible variants turn out to be exalted in the fascinating musical form that is called Theme and Variations. By using the superposition-formalism, we can represent the abstract form of a theme as follows: where: -|μ 0 represents the basic theme (a sharp musical idea, precisely written in the score). -|μ 1 , . . . , |μ n represent the variations of |μ 0 . -|μ represents an ambiguous musical idea that is correlated to the basic theme and to all its variations. Of course the basic theme |μ 0 has a privileged role, while the global theme |μ seems to behave like a kind of "ghost", which is somehow mysteriously present even if it appears hidden. In the sonata-form structure theme often appears both in a major and in a minor variant. In the case of a "simple" situation we can write: where |μ represents a vague musical idea that is common to its major variant |μ + and to its minor variant |μ -. Among the many different examples that might be mentioned let us choose the wonderful incipit of Schubert's last piano sonata in B flat major (D. 960). We find here a somewhat unusual sequence in the presentation of a major and of a minor variant of the first theme of the sonata's first movement. At the very beginning the first theme is exposed in a major form (Fig. 1). Then the theme is repeated with a slight change, after a mysterious trill played by the left hand in a foreign tonality. Soon after (before the appearance of the movement's second theme) the first theme is immediately transformed into a minor mode (Fig. 2), creating a kind of anticipation of the musical events that will be later disclosed during the movement's development. Is it possible to determine, in a natural way, the coefficients c i that occur in a musical superposition |μ ? As is well known, in quantum theory the amplitudes occurring in a superposition i c i |ψ i play an important mathematical and physical role, being responsible, for instance, of the characteristic quantum-interference phenomena. It is not reasonable to expect that the whole range of quantum amplitudes can be interestingly used in the case of musical superpositions. At the same time, given a musical context (say, a musical phrase ore a whole sonata's movement) one can conventionally choose some real numbers that somehow measure the "weight" of different musical features occurring in that context. As an example, consider again a "major-minor superposition" In such a case, the number c 1 can be naturally correlated with the frequency of occurrences of major variants of the musical idea |μ in the context under consideration. In a similar way, the number c 2 will be connected with the minor variants. Tonal ambiguities, in general, can be analyzed by using convenient "musical amplitudes". As is well known, for any scale of the tempered system, the membership-relation is exactly determined (like in classical set theory): any single note either belongs or does not belong to a given scale. Such sharp situation (based on the excluded-middle principle) is, instead, generally violated in the case of musical phrases (which consist of many notes). As Fig. 1 The sonata's first theme in a major mode Fig. 2 A variant of the first theme in a minor mode an example, consider again the first theme of Schubert's last piano-sonata (Fig. 1). Almost all notes of the theme belong to the basic tonality (B flat major) with a single exception: a foreign note (a natural E) that appears in the third measure, creating a brief dissonant chord. This seems to express a fleeting allusion to a "tonal doubt" that is, however, immediately rejected in the same measure, when the natural E disappears, being replaced by the "right" E flat. Should we try to represent the musical idea corresponding to Schubert's theme as a tonality-superposition, we could naturally choose for the amplitude associated to the tonality B flat a real number c i such that |c i | 2 is "very close" to 1 (although from 1). It is worth-while noticing that we are not using here the term "tonality-superposition" in the sense of "polytonality". A typical polytonal phrase consists of distinct parts that belong to different tonalities and are performed at the same time. Quantum superpositions instead express some global forms of tonal ambiguity that vaguely allude to different tonalities. So far we have considered musical amplitudes that are "objectively" grounded on the harmonic structure of a given composition. One could also investigate possible correlations between musical amplitudes and subjective responses to tonal ambiguities, in the framework of appropriate psychological experiments. In this connection, an interesting study might concern, for instance, the emergence of "harmonic illusions" that are, to a certain extent, similar to optical illusions.<Extra-Musical Meanings and Vague Possible Worlds>As is well known, an important feature of music is the capacity of evoking extra-musical meanings: subjective feelings, situations that are vaguely imagined by the composer or by the interpreter or by the listener, real or virtual theatrical scenes (which play an essential role in the case of lyric operas and of Lieder). The interplay between musical ideas and extramusical meanings can be naturally represented in the framework of our quantum semantics, where extra-musical meanings can be dealt with as special examples of vague possible worlds. We can refer to the abstract tensor product of two spaces M Space ⊗ W Space, where: -MSpace represents the space of musical ideas |μ . -W Space represents the space of vague possible worlds, dealt with as special examples of abstract objects |w that can be evoked by musical ideas. Following the quantum-theoretic formalism, we can distinguish between factorized and non-factorized global musical ideas. As expected, a factorized global musical idea will have the form: But we might also meet "Bell-like" entangled global musical ideas, having the form: In the case of lyric operas and of Lieder musical ideas and vague possible worlds are, in fact, always entangled (in an intuitive sense). We need only think how some opera-librettos may appear naive and, in some parts, even funny, if they are read as pieces of theatre, separated from music. Also Lieder, whose texts have often been written by great authors (Goethe, Schiller, Heine, etc.) give rise to similar entangled situations. Generally a musical intonation of a given poem transforms the text into a new global semantic object that somehow absorbs and renews all meanings of the original literary work. The interplay between musical ideas and vague possible worlds gives rise to some special semantic correlations in Wagner's operas, where Leitmotive play an essential role. As is well known, a Leitmotiv is a theme that may be semantically associated to a character or to a place or to a situation or to a subjective feeling. In the structure of an opera, each Leitmotiv appears with different musical and theatrical "masks", and is characterized by a high degree of mutability, which allows continuous transformations and correlations with other Leitmotive. Any appearance of a Leitmotiv involves: 1. A musical idea that corresponds to a theme. 2. A theatrical situation that can be represented as a vague possible world (described by the opera's libretto and evoked by the corresponding musical idea). Sometimes a particular instance of a Leitmotiv has the role of bringing into light events that are not yet known either by the characters or by the audience, possibly anticipating future events. A significant example occurs in the first Act of Die Walküre (the second opera of Der Ring des Nibelungen), when Siegmund is telling Sieglinde and Hunding about the disappearance of his father. He ignores that his father is Wotan himself. But suddenly, the orchestra plays (pianissimo) the Walhall-theme, musically revealing the true identity of Siegmund's father. The Leitmotiv-technique creates some very special effects, bringing into light the similarities between the developing of the musical ideas and the flowing of our (conscious or unconscious) thoughts. Of course, effects of this kind do not concern Wagner's music only. One is dealing with some deep and complicated cognitive phenomena that are today investigated in the framework of neuro-sciences. Perhaps a progress in the neuro-scientific research will allow us to understand (at least to a certain extent) some of the reasons why music represents a kind of universal thought, which is deeply connected with the sphere of our emotions.

title: An Immune Quantum Communication Model for Dephasing Noise Using Four-Qubit Cluster State
abstract: Quantum secure communication of dephasing in the presence of noise is a hot spot in research in the field of quantum secure communication. Quantum steganography aims is to transfer secret information in public quantum channel. But because effect of annealing phase noise, quantum states which is need to transfer easily delayed or changed. So, quantum steganography is very meaning apply to transmit secret information covertly in quantum noisy channels. The article introduced dephasing noise impact on the physics of quantum state, through the theoretical research, construct the logic of quantum states to back the phase noise immunity, and construct the decoherence free subspace, It can guarantees fidelity secret information exchange through quantum communication model in a noisy environment.

title: A New Quantum Proxy Multi-signature Scheme Using Maximally Entangled Seven-Qubit States
abstract: In this paper, we propose a new secure quantum proxy multi-signature scheme using seven-qubit entangled quantum state as quantum channels, which may have applications in e-payment system, e-government, e-business, etc. This scheme is based on controlled quantum teleportation. The scheme uses the physical characteristics of quantum mechanics to guarantee its anonymity, verifiability, traceability, unforgetability and undeniability.
text: <title>A New Quantum Proxy Multi-signature Scheme Using Maximally Entangled Seven-Qubit States<abstract>In this paper, we propose a new secure quantum proxy multi-signature scheme using seven-qubit entangled quantum state as quantum channels, which may have applications in e-payment system, e-government, e-business, etc. This scheme is based on controlled quantum teleportation. The scheme uses the physical characteristics of quantum mechanics to guarantee its anonymity, verifiability, traceability, unforgetability and undeniability.<Introduction>Digital signature, which is an important branch of cryptography, has been widely used in practical applications. Unfortunately, most existing classical signature schemes whose security depends on the difficulty of solving some hard mathematical problems were threatened by quantum computation. Therefore, researchers turn to investigate its quantum counterpart with the hope that quantum signature can become an alternative to classical signature and provide unconditional security. In 1996, Mambo, Usuda, and Okamoto introduced the concept of a proxy signature scheme [1]. It allows a designated person, called a proxy signer, to sign on behalf of an original signer, in case of say, temporal absence, lack of time or computational power, etc. Proxy signatures are useful constructions in grid computing, mobile agent, mobile communications, e-commerce etc. Then, Barnum et al. [2] pointed out a no-go theorem for the application of the quantum signature in 2002. Although Barnum et al.'s conclusion created a serious obstacle for quantum signature, the study of the quantum signature scheme has not stopped. In 2002, Zeng and Keitel [3] first proposed an arbitrated quantum signature (AQS) protocol, which is called the ZK protocol, to sign a quantum message. This work gave an elementary model to overcome Barnum et al.'s no-go theorem for quantum signature [2]. Afterwards, Li et al. found that the arbitrator is unnecessary to entangle with the other two participants in the AQS scheme presented in Ref. [4], and thus the three-particle entangled GHZ states used in the scheme can be replaced with two-particle entangled Bell states. Wen et al. [5,6] proposed some multisignature schemes. Besides, many quantum signature schemes based on quantum mechanics or quantum computing algorithm were proposed [7][8][9][10][11][12]. Quantum entanglement is a key element for applications of quantum communications and quantum information. In particular, the entanglement can be used as a quantum resource to carry out a number of computational and information processing tasks. Due to its great relevance, from both the theoretical and the practical points of view, it is imperative to explore and characterize all aspects of the quantum entanglement of multipartite quantum systems. In this paper we present a quantum proxy multi-signature scheme based on controlled quantum teleportation. A highly entangled seven-qubit state functions as quantum channels. In our scheme, one particle of the entangled seven-qubit state is delivered to the proxy signer Alice, and the original signers Charlie and David hold five particles, while one particle to the verifier Bob. Alice performs Bell-state measurement(BM) on particle 1 and the particle M carrying message, and then Charlie performs single particle measurement on her particles and David perform BM on their particles. Bob could verify the signature according to the correlation of the entangled seven-qubit state. If some disagreement happens, the message owner Alice could be traced. We use quantum key distribution and one-time pad to guarantee the unconditional security and signature anonymity. It is shown to be unconditionally secure, i.e., may not be forged or modified in any way by the receiver or attacker. In addition, it may neither be disavowed by the signatory, nor be deniable by the receiver.<Preliminary Theory>The quantum proxy multi-signature scheme is based on controlled quantum teleportation. In this section, we will introduce the controlled teleportation scheme using seven-qubit entanglement states [13] as quantum channel. Maximally multi-qubit entangled states (MMES) [14] are states whose entanglement is maximal for every (balanced) bipartition. In maximally entangled seven-qubit states, marginal density matrices for subsystems of one and two qubits are completely mixed and most, but not all, of the marginal density matrices of three qubits are completely mixed. The highly entangled seven-qubit state plays a key role in quantum information processing tasks and turns out to be an important resource in quantum communication. This has the form: In the quantum proxy signature, the proxy signer Alice owns particle 1. Particles (2,5,7) and (3,4) are belong to the original signers Charlie and David, respectively. The verifier Bob holds particle 6. Suppose that the quantum state of particle M carrying message in Alice is in which b = 1 and b = -1 reponse to messages M(i) = 1 and M(i) = 0, respectively. The combined state | M1234567 of the whole system composed of particles M and (1,2,3,4,5,6,7) is given by The controlled quantum teleportation works in the following process. (2.1) Alice performs Bell-state measurement on particles (M,1). The four Bell states of 2-qubit are When David measuring outcome on particles (34) is |φ M1 -, particle 6 will be projected into the following state (2.5) According to Alice's, Charlie's and David's measuring outcomes, Bob can impose an appropriate unitary operation U exa on particle 6 to successfully reconstruct the original unknown quantum state |ψ M . For example, when particle 6 is in the states of (6), the unitary operations is Alice successfully transmits the unknown quantum state |ψ M to the receiver Bob under Charlie's and David's control.<Quantum Proxy Multi-signature Scheme>The proposed quantum proxy multi-signature scheme includes the following several phases. Charlie and David are original signers. They delegate a proxy signer Alice to sign message instead of themselves. Bob is the verifier.<Security Analysis and Discussion>In this section, we will display that our proxy signature scheme has the characteristics of classical security and quantum security. An attacker or eavesdropper Eve wants to forge Alice's signature. However, she can not know the key K AB shared between Alice and Bob to produce the signature S A . In the signature procedure, it is impossible for Eve to know the message m. Hence, the behavior of Eve can not be passed in the verifying phase. (4.1. 3) The message owner can be traced Alice sends messages to Charlie and David. Since the messages include the secret keys which are only known by Alice and Charlie or Alice and David, Alice can not disavow her messages m. Once some disagreement happens, according to the parameters of messages and secret keys, combined with the measurement results of particles, the referee can trace the message owner and judge whether the proxy signature is valid or not.<Conclusions>In this paper, we present a quantum proxy multi-signature scheme based on seven-qubit entanglement state. Different from previous quantum signature scheme in classical cryptography, the security of our scheme is guaranteed by the quantum one-time pad and quantum key distribution. Hence, it is unconditionally secure. Seven-qubit entangled states play a key role in quantum information processing tasks. Our scheme can be realized in practice, because it is based on some current developed quantum and classical technologies (teleportation, QKD, quantum encryption).

title: A Quantum Multi-proxy Blind Signature Scheme Based on Genuine Four-Qubit Entangled State
abstract: In this paper, we propose a multi-proxy blind signature scheme based on controlled teleportation. Genuine four-qubit entangled state functions as quantum channel. The scheme uses the physical characteristics of quantum mechanics to implement delegation, signature and verification. The security analysis shows the scheme satisfies the security features of multi-proxy signature, unforgeability, undeniability, blindness and unconditional security.

The security analysis shows the scheme satisfies the security features of multi-proxy signature, unforgeability, undeniability, blindness and unconditional security.<Introduction>Digital signature is one of the most important components of modern cryptography, which serves as a basic module to design cryptography protocols [1], and it has been widely used in electronic commerce and other related fields. Unfortunately, the classical signature schemes are always based on computation complexity, and these schemes could easily be broken with the development of quantum information technology [2]. In addition, assume that Eve could get the secret keys K BU j and K BC , he intercepts the signature β U j and β Cj , tampering with the corresponding signature β U j and β Cj , the following analysis will show the forgery will be impossible. To the message M(i), we suppose U j 's individual signature is |GH Z + M12 , Charlie's measurement result is |1 4 . In order to express easily, we denote S j (i) = {|GH Z + M12 , |1 4 , |SN j }, according to the theory of controlled quantum teleportation, Bob will perform the operation σ x on particle 3. If Eve tampers with S j (i) = {|GH Z - M12 , |0 4 , |SN j }, as is shown in Fig. 3, Bob will perform operation σ z to get the quantum state ), Bob will get the wrong message M(i) = 0(m(i) = -1) by measuring | i M in the basis {|+ , |-}, then he will terminate the scheme. Similarly, if M(i) = 0(m(i) = -1), Bob will obviously detect Eve's behaviour. Furthermore, if Eve tampers with S j (i) = {|H + M12 , |0 4 , |SN j } , he will successfully get the correct message and forge M(i) s signature with a probability 1/7. As the message M = {M(1), M(2), • • • , M(n)}, so he will attack the scheme with a probability 1/7 n . Further, there are t proxy signers, so the scheme will be attacked successfully with a small probability 1/7 tn . So the probability of success is negligible and the signature cannot be forged. In the multi-proxy blind signature scheme, Alice, U j and Charlie sends the messages with the secret keys, such that they cannot deny their signatures and messages. For example, U j sends S U j encrypted by K BU j to Bob, if disputes happen, Bob could get and measure the quantum state |SN j to know the number SN j . So Bob could detect Fig. 3 Two situations of with and without Eve which member of the proxy signers has disavowed the signature. Similarly, Alice and Charlie could not deny the message or the signature. In our scheme, although the proxy signer and signs the message by measuring his particles, he does not know the content of the message. On the one hand, U j does not know that Bob will use the basis {|+ , |-} to get the message M(i), once U j measures his particles in other bases, the correlation of entangled qubits will be destroyed and Bob will get the wrong message. On the other hand, even if U j does know it, the message transformation rule in 2.1 is secret to him. The unconditional security of our scheme is ensured by secret key distribution (BB84 protocol), secure quantum transmission channel and one-time pad algorithm. Additionally, considering the characteristics of the four-qubit entangled state, the distribution of particles in the entangled state is not confined to the method used in the above scheme. Here, we put forward another division of the four particles: the particles (1,2) can also be distributed to Alice, and Charlie holds particle 3, Bob holds particle 4. Similarly, the signature scheme can be finished and proved secure.(We will not repeat the details of the signature scheme.)<Conclusion>In this paper, we present a quantum multi-proxy blind signature scheme based on genuine four-qubit entangled state. Different from the previous signature schemes in classical cryptography, the security of our scheme is guaranteed by the quantum one-time pad and quantum key distribution. Different from the quantum signature proposed in Refs. [19,20], our scheme is based on genuine four-qubit entangled state with less resource, and satisfies the security features of multi-proxy blind signature which has a better application. Furthermore, GH Z-state measurement and single particle measurement are proposed in our scheme. Therefore, our scheme can be implemented with current technologies and experimental conditions and it has a more extensive application value.

title: Controlled Secure Direct Communication with Six-Qubit Entangled States
abstract: We propose an experimentally feasible scheme for implementing controlled quantum secure direct communication by using six-qubit entangled states. According to the results measured by the sender and the controller, the receiver can obtain different secret messages in a deterministic way with unit successful probability. In our scheme, the information-carrying qubits do not need to be transmitted over the public channel. Therefore, the scheme is determinate and secure.

According to the results measured by the sender and the controller, the receiver can obtain different secret messages in a deterministic way with unit successful probability. Therefore, the scheme is determinate and secure.<Introduction>Quantum key distribution (QKD) allows two remote users to share a random key secure, it has been the most famous application of quantum cryptography. Since the first standard QKD scheme was proposed in 1984, QKD has attracted widespread attention and progressed quickly [1][2][3][4][5][6] Quantum secure direct communication (QSDC) is another branch of quantum cryptography. Since the first QSDC scheme based on the basis of the QKD was presented [7] QSDC have been investigated extensively [8][9][10][11]. In this work we propose a new controlled QSDC scheme by using six-qubit entangled states with no need for the second transmission, and it can be achieved only based on local Bell-state measurements. In our scheme, the qubits carrying the secret message do not need to be transmitted between two communicators in public channel, thus the scheme is completely secure if perfect quantum channels are used. And the security of the protocol is also discussed<Controlled QSDC Scheme Using Six-Gubit Entangled States>To achieve the purpose of controlled QSDC, we choose a six-qubit entangled state for our purpose, which is given by where . Here the qubits 1, 2 belong to the sender Alice, the qubits 3, 4 belong to the receiver Bob, and the qubits 5, 6 the controlling qubits belong to Charlie. Now let us describe the scheme in detail as follows: (1) The sender Alice and the receiver Bob want to direct communication, and then they agree the coding method with Bell state as follows: (2) Alice prepares an ordered sequence of six-qubit entangled states ψ i 123456 and enough one-qubit states. The six-qubit entangled states are used as quantum channel, and the one-qubit states are used for generating interference. Then Alice should divide the ordered sequence of six-qubit entangling states into three ordered sequences. The first ordered sequence, called the sequence P i 12 , is composed of qubits 1 and 2 from each six-qubit entangling state, the second ordered sequence P i 34 is composed of qubits 3 and 4, the remaining qubits compose the another ordered sequence P i 56 . In our approach, Alice reserves P i 12 , and sends P i 56 and P i 34 to Charlie and Bob, respectively. For sake of against eavesdropping, these qubits of one-qubit states are arbitrarily mixed in the sequence P i 34 and it's position are known by Alice before P i 34 is sent to Bob. One of modes for mixing one qubit states in the sequence P i 34 is shown in Fig. 1. And then Alice sends P i 56 to Charlie by using the same method. (3) After confirming that Charlie and Bob have received the entire sequence, Alice tells the positions of disturbing one-qubit states to Charlie and Bob. Thus Charlie and Bob find out these disturbing one-qubit states and discard them. (4) Alice randomly chooses sufficient qubits 1 and 2 from P i 12 to apply the single-qubit measurements in the basis of {|0 , |1 }. Then Alice tells the positions and measured Fig. 1 The sketch of mixing one-qubit results for each sampling qubits to Bob and Charlie. Corresponding to the positions in the sequence P i 56 , Charlie make the single-qubit measurements in the basis of {|0 , |1 } on his qubits. With the information, Bob measures the corresponding qubits 3 and 4 in the sequence P i 34 under the basis of {|0 , |1 } and compares the outcomes with Charlie's and Alice's. If their outcomes are completely correlated according to (1), Charlie can sure that the quantum channel is security and continue to the next step. Otherwise, they must abandon the communication and repeat the procedure from the beginning. (5) After ensure the quantum channel is secure, Alice prepares the Bell states ± i ab or ± i ab , which corresponding encoding information are 00, 01, 10 and 11. Then Alice performs the Bell-state measurements on the qubit pairs (a, 1) and (b, 2), and sends the result to Bob and Charlie by classical channel. (6) Finally, Bob makes the Bell-state measurements on the qubits (3,4), and Charlie performs the single-qubit measurements on the qubits in the basis {|0 , |1 }, respectively, and compares with their outcome results and Alice's result. And Bob can get the secret information from Alice under the collaboration of Charlie. To make the encoding and decoding process more clear, we give an example for explain our scheme: we suppose Alice wants to send classical information 00. First Alice prepares a quantum state + ab , and performs the Bell-state measurements on the qubit pairs (a, 1) and (b, 2), and then sends the result to Bob and Charlie. At last, Bob makes the Bell-state measurements on the qubits (3,4) and Charlie performs two single-qubit measurements on the qubits (5,6), and compare the qubits parts (a, 1), (b, 2), (3,4) and (5,6) outcomes results to get the information 00 from Alice. The theory and all of results are shown as follows: And the same, Alice wants to transmit information 11, 01 or 10, she would prepares the quantum state as + ab , + ab or - ab , respectively; then she measures (a, 1) and (b, 2) qubits pairs on the Bell basis and sends the result to Bob and Charlie. And then Charlie performs two single-qubit measurements on the qubits (5,6), and tells the result to Bob. After that, Bob to decode the secret information by measuring qubit pair (3,4) on Bell basis, and analyzes these outcomes result. Decoding table and all of outcomes shown as Table 1. Judging from the Table 1, we propose communication solution have an advantages, the qubits carrying information no need to transmit on public channel. Therefore Eve cannot get any secret information in all of the communication process. measurements on the qubits at hand. And then Charlie performs two single-qubit measurements on his own qubits. At last, Bob can decode the secret information after making the Bell-state measurements on his qubits and analysing all of results from Alice and Bob. And we show this controlled QSDC scheme may be determinate and secure.

title: Dynamics of Measurement-Induced Non-Locality and Geometric Measure of Discord in a Two-Qubit Heisenberg XY Chain
abstract: By taking into account the Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya (DM) interaction under uniform magnetic field, quantum correlation behaviors measured by the measurement-induced nonlocality (MIN) and the geometric measure of discord (GMOD) in a two-qubit XY model are investigated in detail. Turning the different parameters can lead the two kinds of measurements to present different properties. For example, increasing the parameter B(uniform magnetic field), the existing region of MIN is larger than GMOD; MIN can appear the phenomenon of monotonous reduction when the parameter D(Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interaction) is smaller than one threshold value, while GMOD cannot; MIN monotonously reduces with enhancive value of T(temperature), while GMOD initial experiences a slightly increasing and then decreases. One interesting point is that the more obvious and complicated difference between them are shown from the initial values. This property is both true for the zero temperature and the finite temperature. Through analyzing the limit case of the temperature approaching zero, the analytic solutions give the detailed reasons why have different effect on the initial values. Moreover, from the analytic solutions, we know the initial value of MIN is always larger than or equal to GMOD.

Turning the different parameters can lead the two kinds of measurements to present different properties. For example, increasing the parameter B(uniform magnetic field), the existing region of MIN is larger than GMOD; MIN can appear the phenomenon of monotonous reduction when the parameter D(Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya interaction) is smaller than one threshold value, while GMOD cannot; MIN monotonously reduces with enhancive value of T(temperature), while GMOD initial experiences a slightly increasing and then decreases. This property is both true for the zero temperature and the finite temperature. Through analyzing the limit case of the temperature approaching zero, the analytic solutions give the detailed reasons why have different effect on the initial values. Moreover, from the analytic solutions, we know the initial value of MIN is always larger than or equal to GMOD.<Introduction>Quantum correlation arises from noncommutativity of operators representing states, observables, and measurements [1]. There are many surprising phenomena in the quantum world. Non-locality is a significant concept in the quantum world without the classical counterpart [2]. Quantum non-locality usually refers to the fact that properties of one particle can be affected by another particle that is sufficiently far away and is widely studied by the violation of Bell in equalities [3][4][5][6][7]. Quantum entanglement, which refers to the inseparability of the states, is very important in quantum information processing and can be realized in many kinds of physical systems which involve quantum correlation. Quantum entanglement has been investigated widely in past decades, while other quantum correlation seems to have been seldom exploited before. An alternative classification for quantum correlations, which is based on quantum measurements, has arisen in recent years and also plays an important role in quantum information theory [1,[8][9][10]. In particular, quantum discord (QD) [11] is introduced to measure these quantum correlations. There exist indeed separable mixed states having nonzero discord, and the separable mixed states can be used to perform useful quantum tasks [12]. Evaluation of QD in general requires considerable numerical minimization and analytical expressions are known only for certain classes of states. Recently, Luo and Fu [13] studied the measurement-induced non-locality (MIN) from a geometric perspective based on Von Neumann measurements, which is quite different from the violation of Bell inequalities. The key idea they used is that any disturbance in the system's overall state can be attributed to the genuine nonlocal features of the system when local measurements do not disturb the states of the subsystems. The MIN is intimately related to, but different from the geometric measure of quantum discord (GMOD) [14,15]. However, both MIN and GMOD provide novel classification schemes for bipartite states, and are quantum resources quite different from entanglement. They may be useful in quantitative study of quantum state steering [16], remote state control [17,18], general quantum dense coding [19], and cryptography [20]. Spin is regarded as a suitable candidate of qubits, and the Heisenberg model describes the basic spin-spin interaction. Naturally, this type of model has been extensively studied. However, the spin-spin coupling will not only affect the measurements of the quantum correlation, the spin-orbit coupling will also have an impact on the measurements. It was argued that models of low-dimensional magnetic materials can be supplemented with Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya (DM) interaction, which is arising from the spin-orbit coupling [21]. The DM interaction describes superexchange between the interacting spins, and is known to have many exotic effects on entanglement [22][23][24]. Recently, Liu et al. have shown that the DM interaction weakens the critical behavior in the derivatives of correlations in the infinite XY chain [25]. Motivated by the above knowledges, in this paper, we study the properties of quantum correlation behaviors measured by the measurement-induced nonlocality (MIN) and the geometric measure of discord (GMOD) in two-qubit XY model with taking into account the Dzyaloshinsky-Moriya (DM) interaction under uniform magnetic field. This paper is arranged as follows: In Section 2, introducing the Hamiltonian of two-qubit XY model with DM interaction under uniform magnetic field and giving the thermal state density matrix of the system. In Section 3, briefly review the definitions of the measurementinduced nonlocality (MIN) and the geometric measure of discord (GMOD) firstly, and then investigate the different properties of MIN and GMOD dynamics in detail. Finally Section 4 is devoted to conclusion and discussion.<Description of Quantum Channel>The Hamiltonian of two-qubit XY model with DM interaction (along the z-direction) and uniform magnetic field B (along the z axis) in terms of the raising and lowering operators S ± = S x ± iS y , which can be expressed as: Where J = and γ = J x -Jy J x +J y . J x and J y are the coupling constants along the X and Y axis, respectively. The parameter γ (0< γ <1) measures the anisotropy in the XY plane. The four eigenvalues and the corresponding four eigenstates canbe , where the parameters ξ = B 2 + J 2 γ 2 and η = √ D 2 + J 2 . For a spin system in equilibrium at temperature T , based on knowing the spectrum of H , the thermal state density matrix is ρ(T ) = 1 Z e -βH , where Z = T r e -βH is the partition function and β = 1 k B T (k B is Boltzmann's constant, and usually being set to be unit k B = 1). After some calculations, the density matrix obeys the X-structure and expressed as following These nonzero matrix elements are expressed as following Z cosh(βη), and z(T ) = z * (T ) = -J +iD ηZ sinh(βη), where Z is the partition function given by Z = 2 cosh(βξ ) + 2 cosh(βη). Based on knowing the density matrix of this spin model, one can obtain the quantum correlation properties behavior by using different correlation measures. In the following, we will use two measures of quantum correlation (MIN and GMOD) to study the differences between them with this spin model.<The Definitions and Properties of MIN and GMOD>The concept of MIN was first introduced by Luo and Fu. Let us review their key result in the following. Considering a bipartite state ρ from a and b components with the density matrices ρ a and ρ b , the MIN can be written as where the max is taken over the von Neumann measurements a = a k which do not disturb ρ a locally and satisfy k a k ρ a a k = ρ a . • is the Hilbert-Schmidt norm with X 2 = tr X † X . From this definition we naturally associate MIN with the definition of GMOD Here the min is over all local von Neumann measurements a which is sharply different from the max over locally invariant ones used in defining the MIN in (4). Generally speaking, m × n bipartite state ρ can be expressed as where X i and Y j are the Hermitian operators which are traceless. The is also satisfied. Luo and Fu have figured out an analytical formula of MIN for the (2 × n)-dimensional states where the x = (x 1 , x 2 , x 3 ) T with x = 3 i=1 x 2 i and the R is the real 3 × 3 matrix with elements r ij , λ min is the smallest eigenvalue of RR T , and the expression of GMOD can be written as where the k max is the largest eigenvalue of the matrix xx T + RR T . According to the density matrix and the definition of N(ρ), we can obtain the analytical expression of MIN as According to the density matrix and the definition of D(ρ), the GMOD can be written as With the definitions of quantum correlation measured by MIN and GMOD, we will concentrate our attention on investigating the properties of them. In Fig. 1, it is a plot of measurement-induced non-locality as a function of temperature T with changing different parameters under certain fixed conditions. Figure 1a andb clearly show that changing the values of γ or B can influence the initial value of MIN. Moreover, the larger γ can lead the initial value of MIN to be larger, while the smaller B can make MIN approach the larger initial value. However, from Fig. 1c, it can be discovered that in any case to change the value of D, the initial value of MIN is always invariant. With increasing temperature, the value of MIN is only a monotone decreasing function. Figure 2, with the same condition as Fig. 1, plots the geometric measure of discord as a function of temperature T. From Fig. 2a andb, it can be seen that the different values of γ or B also can effect the initial value of GMOD. The GMOD is the same as the MIN, the larger γ can lead the initial value to achieve the larger one, while the smaller B can make it reach a larger initial value. The initial value of GMOD is also independent of changing the value of D in Fig. 2c. We note that, in Fig. 2a andc, the GMOD experiences raise before reaching the peak value then decreases with enhancive value of temperature which are very different from Fig. 1a andc. Not only the monotonously decreasing curves exist, but also the curve which first increases and then decreases is shown in Fig. 2b. It is evidently found that the initial values of the two kinds of measurements have different influence on changing different parameters. Now we explore the reasons why exist the phenomenon for the two kinds of measurements. We through analyzing the limit case of T → 0 which not only can reveal the fundamental reason but also can make us study clear structures about the MIN and GMOD. In the procession of taking the limit of the density matrix, we clearly find the initial values of two kinds of measurements is subjected effects by η and ξ . In the limit T = 0, for the case ξ > η, the matrix elements are following a From the above three cases of analytical solution MIN and GMOD, we clearly know that the maximum values of the two measurements are 1 2 which is in the case ξ < η. Through calculation, in the case of ξ ≥ η, we can obtain the initial value of MIN is always greater than GMOD. Figure 3 plots the correlation measures MIN and GMOD as a function of the uniform magnetic field B and the temperature T for fixed values of J = 1, D = 0.9 and γ = 0.8. It can be obviously seen that the more close to zero the temperature is, the more different the curves of MIN and GMOD as a function of B is. With enhancive values of B, MIN and GMOD first experience decrease to the minimum value and then undergo increase to the maximum value. However, the decrease of GMOD after the revival procession is more sharply than MIN. In the region of larger T, the value of MIN is invariable whatever changing B, it means that MIN is independent of B for this case, while GMOD initially undergoes a slightly increasing procession and then keeps fixed. The difference between MIN and GMOD as a function of T which are also larger when B is greater than a certain value. In this case, MIN monotonously reduces with enhancive value of T, while GMOD initial experiences a slightly increasing and then decreases. Moreover, with the two measurements as a function of T, we get that Fig. 3a and b echo Figs. 1 and2. From the plot we can clearly see that the existing region of MIN is larger than GMOD. In Fig. 4, with finite temperature T = 0.2, we present the differences between MIN and GMOD behaviors when B and D are variable. When there is no uniform magnetic, MIN remains at the maximum value which is not independent on the influence of D, while GMOD reduces with decreasing value of D. It can be obviously noted that, in the case of B being larger than certain values, D cannot effect MIN or GMOD. Existing the threshold value of D c , when D < D c , MIN diminishes monotonously with the enhancive value of B. However, GMOD cannot appear the phenomenon of monotonous reduction no matter how to change D and GMOD always behaves the revival phenomenon. In order to see the influences about the DM interaction and the coupling constant on MIN and GMOD behaviors, we plot Fig. 5 with the fixed temperature T = 0.1. From Fig. 5a andb, it can be found when D is 2, the two measurements are invariant and keep the maximum values whatever changing γ for this case. One interesting thing is that, the obvious revival phenomenon which MIN presents in the range of the smaller value of γ , while GMOD presents in the scope of the larger value of γ .<Conclusion>In conclusion, using the MIN and GMOD measures, the quantum correlation properties about Two-qubit Heisenberg XY system under the DM interaction and the uniform magnetic field is studied. It is found that the initial values of the two kinds of measurements have different influence on changing different parameters. From the above plots, we know that the different values of γ and B can effect the initial values of MIN and GMOD, while the value of D cannot. Through analyzing the limit case of T → 0, the detailed reasons have been given by the analytic solutions. Moreover, in the case of ξ ≥ η, we can obtain the initial value of MIN is always greater than GMOD. Our study shows that the more closer to zero the temperature is, the more sharply the decrease of GMOD from the revival procession is. At finite temperature, there exist significant differences between MIN and GMOD as the same changed parameters. When there is no uniform magnetic, with the fixed temperature, MIN keeps the maximum value which is independent of the influence of D, while GMOD reduces with decreasing value of D. In addition, the two measurements as a function of D and γ with the fixed T, the obvious revival phenomenon which MIN presents on the contrary with GMOD. From this paper we know that one can through selecting the appropriate environment sythetically to obtain the ideal quantum correlation. And we also know that the definition of quantum correlation measurements are not uniform, different measuring methods can lead different correlation results.

title: Entanglement Teleportation via Two-Qubit Spin Squeezing Model
abstract: Entanglement teleportation via two spins coupled to each other by one axis twisting spin squeezing interaction is investigated. We mainly concentrate on the properties of the channel entanglement, the output entanglement and the teleportation fidelity. It shows that the output entanglement increases linearly with increasing the value of the input entanglement. With the increasing of T, the teleportated entanglement increases sharply from zero to a maximum value and then decreases slowly to zero when the temperature is improved to one threshold value of T (c) , and the threshold value of T (c) increases with the increasing of the input entanglement. When enlarging the external magnetic, F (a) firstly decreases quickly to a minimum value as the critical magnetic field Omega (c) is reached, then it increases abruptly to a maximum value and finally it will be a certain value. Besides, the critical external magnetic Omega (c) increases when mu is larger. For Omega Omega (c) the value of it decreases from a maximum value. The influence of T on the average fidelity is similar with mu.
text: <title>Entanglement Teleportation via Two-Qubit Spin Squeezing Model<abstract>Entanglement teleportation via two spins coupled to each other by one axis twisting spin squeezing interaction is investigated. We mainly concentrate on the properties of the channel entanglement, the output entanglement and the teleportation fidelity. It shows that the output entanglement increases linearly with increasing the value of the input entanglement. With the increasing of T, the teleportated entanglement increases sharply from zero to a maximum value and then decreases slowly to zero when the temperature is improved to one threshold value of T c , and the threshold value of T c increases with the increasing of the input entanglement. When enlarging the external magnetic, F a firstly decreases quickly to a minimum value as the critical magnetic field c is reached, then it increases abruptly to a maximum value and finally it will be a certain value. Besides, the critical external magnetic c increases when μ is larger. For < c the value of the average fidelity increases with the increasing of μ, but for > c the value of it decreases from a maximum value. The influence of T on the average fidelity is similar with μ.<Introduction>Quantum entanglement opens the door to many interesting applications of quantum mechanics in the field of information processing in the last decade. One of the most peculiar and fascinating one is quantum teleportation [1-3, 24-28, 33-38], by which the unknown state of a system can be transmitted from a location to a distant one with the help of local operations and classical communication. In recent years, there has been an ongoing effort to characterize qualitatively and quantitatively the entanglement properties of condensed Yang Guo-Hui yangguohui 1981 1981@126.com 1 School of Physics and Information Engineering, Shanxi Normal University, Linfen 041004, People's Republic of China matter systems and apply them in many fields, such as quantum teleportation, super coding [4], quantum cryptography [5], ect. The quantum entanglement in solid state systems such as spin chains is an important emerging field [6][7][8][9][10][33][34][35][36][37][38]. Spin chains are natural candidates for the realization of entanglement compared with other physics systems. The Heisenberg chain,the simplest spin chain, has been used to construct a quantum computer [11,12]. By suitable coding, the Heisenberg interaction alone can be used for quantum computation [13][14][15]. In addition, quantum teleportation has been extensively investigated both experimentally and theoretically. Since decoherence from the environment always impacts on the degree of entanglement, the resource is approximately near to the real circumstances. As an important source of entanglement, thermal entanglement and entanglement teleportation via thermal entangled states has been widely investigated in many previous studies. We here propose a substance of a pair of spins subject to an external magnetic field and coupled to each other by a so called one-axis twisting nonlinear spin squeezing interaction [16][17][18]. The motivation behind considering this particular interaction is its capability to establish pairwise quantum correlations among the spins. In our this paper, the two spins model under an external magnetic field and coupled to each other by a one-axis twisting spin squeezing interaction served as one dissipative quantum channel for thermal entanglement teleportation is investigated in detail. We consider the input state is a pure two-qubit entangled state. In Section 2, we describe the two spins model, give the spectrum of the Hamiltonian and obtain the density matrix operator, at the same time we calculate the channel entanglement and analyze the effects of above factors on the channel entanglement. In Section 3, we calculate the measure of entanglement for the teleportated state and analyze the parameters on the teleportated entanglement. In Section 4, we derive the average fidelity in the process of thermal entanglement teleportation and analyze its characters. Finally, we conclude our results in Section 5.<Description of the Quantum Channel>In this work, we study the two-spin model under an external magnetic field and coupled to each other by a one-axis twisting spin squeezing interaction. The Hamiltonian operator can be expressed as follows [29,30]: where (≥ 0) is the strength of the external magnetic field in z direction, μ(≥ 0) describes the strength of the spin squeezing interaction in x direction, S α = 1 2 2 i=1 σ i α , (α ∈ x, y, z) are the collective spin operators, and σ i α are the Pauli matrices for the i th spin. The interaction establishes pairwise correlations between all the individual spins in the collective spin system; in our case bipartite correlations are formed between the two spins. For a system of two spins, the eigenvalues E n and the corresponding eigenvectors |ψ n of the Hamiltonian (1) can be caculated as where κ = μ 2 + 4 2 and When thermal fluctuations are introduced into the system, the density matrix of this two spins at thermal equilibrium is ρ = 1 z e -βH = 4 n=1 P n (T )|ψ n ψ n |, where P n (T ) = e -βE n /Z are the occupation probabilities of the eigenstates, β = 1/(kT )(k = 1), T is the temperature, and Z = n e -βE n is the partition function. In the standard basis |11 , |10 , |01 , |00 , the density matrix ρ(T ) can be expressed as The entanglement of two qubits state ρ can be measured by the concurrence C which is written as where the quantities λ i (i = 1 . . . 4) are the square roots of the four eigenvalues of the matrix R = ρSρ * S, ρ is the density matrix and S = σ y 1 ⊗σ y 2 , the symbol * stands for the complex conjugate. The concurrence is available no matter whether ρ is pure or mixed. The concurrence C = 0 corresponds to an unentangled state and C = 1 for a maximally entangled state. We term the entanglement, which measured by concurrence, associated with thermal state ρ(T ) as thermal concurrence. For a density matrix with X-structure as seen above equation, the concurrence between the two qubits is shown in Fig. 1. It demonstrates the dependence of thermal entanglement on the spin squeezing interaction μ and the external magnetic interaction at T = 0.1. We see Fig. 1 Thermal concurrence for the spin channel when T = 0.1. T is plotted in units of the Boltzmann constant k. We work in units where and μ are dimensionless that there is no entanglement when the strength of the spin squeezing interaction in μ or the strength of the external magnetic filed is zero. The channel entanglement increases firstly and then decreases with the increasing of . While the influence of μ on the channel entanglement is different when the external magnetic filed is different. For the smaller value of , the channel entanglement increases firstly and then decreases with the increasing of μ . For the larger value of , the entanglement increases with the increasing of μ. In addition, the maximum value of channel entanglement exists where the value of is about 5. That is to say, weaker or stronger external magnetic field will decrease the channel entanglement.<Thermal Entanglement Teleportation>For the entanglement teleportation of a whole two-qubit system of a mixed state in this spin chains, the standard teleportation through mixed states can be regarded as a general depolarizing channel [19,20]. Similar to the standard teleportation protocol, entanglement teleportation for the mixed channel of an input entangled state is destroyed and its replica state appears at the remote place after applying a local measurement in the form of linear operators. Using the above two-qubit mixed state ρ(t) as a resource, we consider as input a qubit in an arbitrary pure state |ϕ in = cos(θ/2)|10 + e iφ sin(θ/2)|01 , where (0 θ π and 0 φ 2π ). Here the different values of θ describe all states with different amplitudes, and φ are the phase of these states. The entanglement of the input state C in = 2| sin(θ/2) cos(θ/2)| can be measured by the concurrence of Wooters [21].
